newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes chief not seen getting board job - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes chief not seen getting board job - paper.

text.p: Restructuring plans at German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG do not include a job for the head of its Mercedes-Benz unit, a German newspaper said at the weekend, further fanning talk that Helmut Werner may soon quit.

Die Welt am Sonntag reported that the restructuring plans no longer include the position of a vice-chairman which it said is "another indication that Helmut Werner will not become part of the new 10-member board."

Werner had been earmarked to take the second job at Daimler-Benz, but he is also said to oppose the restructuring plans pushed forward by management board chairman Juergen Schrempp because his unit would lose its independence.
Luxury car maker Mercedes is the Daimler's most profitable unit.
Late last week Manager Magazin reported that Werner would leave when Daimler-Benz implements a planned management reorganisation.
The magazine said Werner's departure was agreed in confidential talks in early December between him, Daimler's management board chairman Juergen Schrempp and supervisory board chairman Hilmar Kopper.
Both Mercedes and Daimler declined to comment. A Daimler spokesman said: "The supervisory board (of Daimler) will meet on January 23 to discuss the structure as well as people."
Manager Magazin said Mercedes-Benz AG will be merged into the Daimler-Benz group.
Speculation that Werner could step down has intensified in recent weeks, raising the prospect of what would be a serious loss to the company.
Industry analysts have said Werner's departure would be a blow to Mercedes, which he guided back to profitability with a massive overhaul in model strategy.
The unsourced report in the magazine said Mercedes, which contributes 70 percent to Daimler's sales, would account for five members on the group's new 10-member management board.

The Welt reported the board would include Juergen Hubbert, Kurt Lauk, Dieter Zetsche, Manfred Bischoff, Klaus Mangold, Manfred Gentz, and Eckhard Cordes. Two postions, for personnel and research, have not yet been determined, the paper said.
Juergen Hubbert, in charge of cars, Kurt Lauk, who heads the truck division, and Dieter Zetsche, who is responsible for marketing and sales, are all currently on the Mercedes board.

Manager Magazine earlier said the president of Mercedes-Benz Argentina, Axel Arendt, is likely to become head of personnel at Daimler, taking over from Manfred Gentz who would concentrate exclusively on his responsibilities for finance and controlling.
Michael Kraemer, head of preliminary research at Mercedes-Benz AG, was the main candidate to replace Hartmut Weule as Daimler's management board member in charge of research, Manager Magazine said.
